name: [Portal] Partner websites consume the medailonek API (CZ/SK/HU)
description:
### Summary

The three public partner websites for the Czech, Slovak and Hungarian markets today hold partner profile cards, called medailonky, as content edited by hand in WordPress. After this task they stop being the source of truth and instead display the cards that partners maintain in the Partner Portal and that the CRM exposes through a public read API. Visitors keep the same experience: a list of partners that can be narrowed by category and region, and a detail page for each partner in the language of the given site. Old partner URLs keep working through redirects, and the switch is timed together with the import of existing cards into the CRM, so that no partner disappears from the web during the transition. Which technical option is used, new static microsites or the existing WordPress installations calling the API, is decided by a separate analysis; this task implements the chosen option. The addon marketplace website and any redesign beyond what the chosen option requires are out of scope.

### Why?

Partners will edit their medailonek in the portal, but the change only has value when it appears on the public websites without anybody at Shoptet retyping it. Today the public content is maintained manually in three separate WordPress installations, which is exactly the routine work the portal is meant to remove. Without this connection the portal would publish into the CRM and nowhere visible, and the migrated data would drift apart from the websites again within weeks.

### What?

partneri.shoptet.cz and its Slovak and Hungarian counterparts render the medailonek list and detail pages from the public read API over CRM, each in the language of its site. Visitors can filter the list by partner category and region, and every published partner has a stable detail URL. Partner URLs published before the cutover redirect to the new addresses. Website functions that the inventory from the analysis marks as kept, such as the contact form, continue to work. Once a partner's medailonek is published in the portal, it shows up on the websites without manual intervention.

### Acceptance Criteria

On each of the three partner websites (CZ, SK, HU) the partner list is rendered from the public medailonek read API and shows only medailonky published for that site's language; WordPress no longer holds medailonek content as the source of truth.

The list can be filtered by partner category and by region; for the same parameters the filtered result equals the API response.

Every published partner has a detail page whose content matches the medailonek published in the portal, visible within the refresh interval agreed in the analysis (target: at most 15 minutes after publication).

Every partner URL that existed on the WordPress sites before cutover returns a 301 redirect to the corresponding new detail page (or to the list when the partner is no longer published); verified by crawling the exported URL list with zero 404s.

Cutover happens only after the CRM import is complete and reconciled; a before/after comparison per site shows the same set of published partners (zero partners missing).

Functions marked as kept in the inventory from the analysis (e.g. contact form) work on all three sites after cutover and are verified manually per market.

Automated tests cover the API client and rendering layer of the chosen option; any new PHP in the monorepo passes PHPStan level 10 and any React code passes make fe-test; a smoke test of list, detail and redirects runs against staging for all three sites.

### Open questions

- Wiki Q5: the option (static microsites vs WordPress-on-API) is decided in ; the concrete work breakdown is fixed only after that analysis, therefore the acceptance criteria describe the outcome, not the stack.
- Vendor involvement: whether the microsites vendor implements part of the work, and who owns the sites operationally after go-live.
- Fallback date: the latest date by which the option must be decided so the April 2027 target holds, and what the fallback is if it slips (e.g. WordPress-on-API first, static sites later).

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-16_

- Monorepo references to the partner websites to re-check after cutover (URLs, redirects): `cms/controllers/ShoptetFooterController.php` (footer links to partneri.shoptet.cz / .sk) and storefront templates under `cms/templates/frontend_templates/shoptet_responsive/templates/content/`.
- `cms/packages/Cors/Helper/CorsHeaders.php` allowlists only `SHOPTET_PARTNERS_CZ`; if the sites call the API from the browser, add the SK/HU (or new static) origins.
- `cms/packages/Statistics/Helper/InternalStatsHelper.php` reads partner counts from the WordPress endpoint `partneri.shoptet.cz/wp-json/post-count-api/v2/count` (`partneriPartnersCountCz/Sk`); after cutover rewire to the CRM read API or drop.
- The API contract and field mapping (Wiki Q3) come from ; render from that contract, do not duplicate the mapping on the website side.
- No website code lives in the monorepo; if the static option wins, agree in  where the repository lives, who deploys it and the CODEOWNERS analogue (PartnerPortal paths in cms4 belong to `@shoptet/devrel-team`).
